# Predicting flight delays

We will use a ridge regression model to predict flight delays, more precisely flight **arrival** delays, for flights from the three New York City airports John F Kennedy Intl (JFK), Newark Liberty Intl (EWR), and La Guardia (LGA), based on flight data from 2013 in the `nycflights13` package.

Design assumptions

- We want to predict the destination arrival delays, i.e., our response variable will be the arrival delay, `arr_delay`
- We will exclusively use the flights and weather data available in the `nycflights13` package to develop our model
- The time for prediction is before, or at the latest, time for take-off.


```{r setup}
library(BonusLab)

```

## Flights and weather data

Get flights data:
```{r}
flights_data_raw<-
  nycflights13::flights

flights_data_raw |> dplyr::glimpse(width=50)

flights_data_raw |> 
  dplyr::summarize(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::n_distinct(.))) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
                      names_to =c("variable"), values_to="unique_values") |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(unique_values))
```

Variables not present before take-off (`dep_time`, `dep_delay`, `arr_time`, `air_time`) will not be used as predictors in our model, and are therefore excluded.  

Both `flight` = flight number (notably not a unique identifier for a route), and `tailnum` = a specific aircraft identifier, would be categorical variables with very high cardinality without providing useful predictive information (not generalizable and also largely redundant), and are also excluded.

We observe that there is a redundancy in data when it comes to date-time: `year` carries no useful information since all data enamates from the same year, and both `year`, `month` and `day` are also present in the `time-hour` variable. Knowing that representing month-day can be tricky (especially taking into consideration that 12-31 and 01-01 actually are very close, not at a 365 distance away) we choose to represent day-of-year using a Fourier encoding, a harmonic regression with k=2 harmonics (see <https://otexts.com/fpp3/advanced.html>), which is capable of capturing annual and biannual seasonality as well as a smooth transition from New Years Eve. This will generate four variables, `doy_sin1`, `doy_cos1`, `doy_sin2`, and `doy_cos2`, but `year`, `month`, and `day` will be dropped.

Turning to time variables we choose to exclude `minute` (= minute in the scheduled departure time) since that variable represents a too high granuality to be meningful. For the same reason we rename `hour` (= hour in scheduled departure time) to `hour_dep`, and extract the hour in scheduled arrival time (into `hour_arr`), and then we exclude `sched_dep_time` and `sched_arr_time.` 

Keeping the `hour_dep` and `hour_arr` as numerical variables would not take into account the 24 cycle, and also a change of one hour can inlfuence arrival delays in different ways at different times of the day. The v`hour_dep` and `hour_arr` variables could alternatively be converted into factors, or be subjected to the same type of Fourier encoding as we use for day-of-year. At this stage we add both variants to the data tibble, having them ready to use for comparison.

Since we will use `time-hour` for data joining it is kept for now, but will be dropped later.

```{r}
flights_data <- 
  flights_data_raw |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    doy = lubridate::yday(time_hour), # 1-365, used temporarily
    doy_sin1 = sin(2 * pi * doy / 365),
    doy_cos1 = cos(2 * pi * doy / 365),
    doy_sin2 = sin(4 * pi * doy / 365),
    doy_cos2 = cos(4 * pi * doy / 365)) |> 
  dplyr::rename(hour_dep = hour) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(hour_arr = (sched_arr_time %/% 100) %% 24, .after = hour_dep) |>
  # Fourier encoding of hour variables
    dplyr::mutate(
    hour_dep_sin1 = sin(2 * pi * hour_dep / 24), # departure hour
    hour_dep_cos1 = cos(2 * pi * hour_dep / 24),
    hour_dep_sin2 = sin(4 * pi * hour_dep / 24),
    hour_dep_cos2 = cos(4 * pi * hour_dep / 24),
    hour_arr_sin1 = sin(2 * pi * hour_arr / 24), # arrival hour
    hour_arr_cos1 = cos(2 * pi * hour_arr / 24),
    hour_arr_sin2 = sin(4 * pi * hour_arr / 24),
    hour_arr_cos2 = cos(4 * pi * hour_arr / 24)) |> 
  # hour variables as factors
  dplyr::mutate(hour_dep_f = factor(hour_dep),
                hour_arr_f = factor(hour_arr)) |>
  
  # variable exclusion
  dplyr::select(!c(dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, air_time, flight, tailnum, 
                     year, month, day, doy, minute, sched_dep_time, sched_arr_time))
```


Get weather data:
```{r}
weather_data_raw <- 
  nycflights13::weather 
weather_data_raw |> dplyr::glimpse(width=50)

```

The variables `year`, `month`, `day` and `hour` in weather_data are all excluded, since `time_hour` sufficiently identifies date-time for each observation. The weather data are overall continuous, which means we don't have any cardinality issues here.

```{r}
weather_data <- 
  weather_data_raw |> 
  dplyr::select(!c(year, month, day, hour))
```


Flights and weather data are then joined into one data set, using the common variables `origin` and `time-hour`, the latter is removed when the data sets are joined. The resulting tibble is checked for missing values (variables with zero missing values are filtered out):

```{r}
flights_and_weather_data <- 
  flights_data |> 
  dplyr::left_join(weather_data, by = dplyr::join_by(origin, time_hour)) |> 
  dplyr::select(!time_hour)

flights_and_weather_data |>
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(everything(), 
                          list(missing = ~ sum(is.na(.)), 
                               percent = ~ round(mean(is.na(.))*100, digits =1))))|>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
                      names_to =c("measure",".value"), names_pattern = "^(.*)_(missing|percent)$") |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(missing)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(missing>0)
```

The variable `wind_gust` is excluded due to the high proportion of missing values. Also, all rows where `arr_delay` is missing are removed since this is our response variable. 

In line with how we handle day-of-year and hours, we use a sine-cosine encoding for `wind_dir`, the wind direction, in a similar way since wind directions 1° and 359° are very close, not the opposite).

With the join in place, the inherently categorical variables `carrier`, `origin`, and `dest` are converted to factors. Our assessment is that this does not constitute a data leakage, since the set of carriers, origins and destinations can be retrieved from domain information, i.e., outside the current data material.

```{r}
flights_and_weather_data <-
  flights_and_weather_data |>
  dplyr::select(!wind_gust) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(arr_delay)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    wind_dir_sin = sin(wind_dir * pi / 180),
    wind_dir_cos = cos(wind_dir * pi / 180)) |>
  dplyr::select(!wind_dir) |> 
  # categorical predictors as factors
  dplyr::mutate(
    carrier = factor(carrier),
    origin = factor(origin),
    dest = factor(dest)) 
```

## Data set partitioning

The data set is split into 80% for training, 15 % for validation and 5% for test.

```{r}
set.seed(739228)

# 80% training ()
train_indices <- 
  caret::createDataPartition(flights_and_weather_data$arr_delay, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)

train_data <- flights_and_weather_data[train_indices, ]
remaining_data <- flights_and_weather_data[-train_indices, ]

# Split remaining data into validation and test
validation_indices <- caret::createDataPartition(
  remaining_data$arr_delay,
  p = 0.75, # 75% out of 20% = 15%
  list = FALSE
)

validation_data <- remaining_data[validation_indices, ]
test_data <- remaining_data[-validation_indices, ]
```

## Imputation

We re-check the now final, undivided data set for NA occurence, and then we replace NA occurences with training data medians in all data partitions (to avoid data leak).

```{r}

##### imputation helper function #####
impute_medians <-  function(data, medians){
  data_imp <-
    data |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(names(medians)),
                         ~ dplyr::replace_values(., NA 
                                            ~ medians[[dplyr::cur_column()]])))
}

# missing data check for the current full data set
misssing_data_overview <- 
  flights_and_weather_data |>
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(everything(), 
                          list(missing = ~ sum(is.na(.)), 
                               percent = ~ round(mean(is.na(.))*100, 
                                                 digits =1)))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
                      names_to =c("measure",".value"), names_pattern = "^(.*)_(missing|percent)$") |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(missing)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(missing>0)

# compute train data medians for non-complete columns in the full data set
train_medians <- 
  train_data |>
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(misssing_data_overview$measure), 
                   ~ median(., na.rm = TRUE)))

# impute

train_data_imp <- 
  impute_medians(train_data, train_medians)

validation_data_imp <- 
  impute_medians(validation_data, train_medians)

test_data_imp <- 
  impute_medians(test_data, train_medians)

# imputation check, expecting no NA:s left
sum(is.na(train_data_imp))
sum(is.na(validation_data_imp))
sum(is.na(test_data_imp))

# XXXXX


```


## Training of ridge regression models


```{r}
#ridgereg_KA

ridgereg <- function(formula, data, lambda){

  stopifnot("formula argument must be formula object" =
              inherits(formula, "formula"),
            "data argument must be a data frame (or tibble)" =
              is.data.frame(data),
            "lambda argument must be a single non-negative number" =
              is.numeric(lambda) && length(lambda) == 1 && lambda >= 0)

  ### extract model
  # create a model/design matrix from the formula and data
  X <- model.matrix(formula, data) # independent variables

  # extract the depedent variable from data using formula names
  y_name <- all.vars(formula)[1]
  y <- data[[y_name]]

  # keep the call
  call_arg <- match.call()

  ### normalize covariates (the intercept column is left as is)
  is_intercept <- colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"
  x_mean <- colMeans(X[, !is_intercept, drop = FALSE])
  x_sd <- apply(X[, !is_intercept, drop = FALSE], 2, sd)

  ############

  invalid_sd <- !is.finite(x_sd) | x_sd == 0

  if (any(invalid_sd)) {
    stop(
      "Cannot standardize predictors with zero or invalid SD: ",
      paste(names(x_sd)[invalid_sd], collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  ############
  X[, !is_intercept] <-
    scale(X[, !is_intercept, drop = FALSE], center = x_mean, scale = x_sd)

  ### calculate ridge regression statistics (least squares)
  # penalty matrix, lambda * I with no penalty on the intercept
  penalty <- diag(lambda, ncol(X))
  penalty[is_intercept, is_intercept] <- 0

  # beta_hat = (X^T X + lambda I)^-1 X^T y
  beta_hat <- solve(crossprod(X) + penalty, crossprod(X, y))
  rownames(beta_hat) <- colnames(X)

  # y_hat = fitted values
  y_hat <- X %*% beta_hat

  ### create a ridgereg object
  ridgereg_obj <-
    structure(
      list(
        formula = formula,
        call_arg = call_arg,
        lambda = lambda,
        X = X,
        y = y,
        y_name = y_name,
        x_mean = x_mean,
        x_sd = x_sd,
        beta_hat = beta_hat,
        y_hat = y_hat),
      class = "ridgereg")

  return(ridgereg_obj)
}

```

```{r}

potential_predictors <- setdiff(names(train_data_imp),"arr_delay")

common_predictors <- potential_predictors[
  !startsWith(potential_predictors, "hour")
]

hour_predictors <- list(
  numeric = c("hour_dep", "hour_arr"),
  factor = c("hour_dep_f", "hour_arr_f"),
  fourier = c(
    "hour_dep_sin1", "hour_dep_cos1",
    "hour_dep_sin2", "hour_dep_cos2",
    "hour_arr_sin1", "hour_arr_cos1",
    "hour_arr_sin2", "hour_arr_cos2"
  )
)

# create three model formulas (with each different hours representation) 
model_formulas <- 
  purrr::map(hour_predictors, 
             function(hours)
               stats::reformulate(c(common_predictors, hours),
                                  response ="arr_delay"))

# checking the design matrices have the same order of predictor columns, 
# and all rows retained
design_compatibility <- 
  purrr::map(
  model_formulas,
  function(f) {
    X_train <- stats::model.matrix(f, train_data_imp)
    X_val   <- stats::model.matrix(f, validation_data_imp)
    X_test  <- stats::model.matrix(f, test_data_imp)

    c(validation = identical(colnames(X_train), colnames(X_val)),
      test = identical(colnames(X_train), colnames(X_test)),
      train_rows = nrow(X_train) == nrow(train_data_imp),
      validation_rows = nrow(X_val) == nrow(validation_data_imp),
      test_rows = nrow(X_test) == nrow(test_data_imp))
  })

design_compatibility

# creating a lambda grid
# lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-2, 5, length.out = 20)
# lambda_grid_small <- 10^seq(-6, -2, length.out = 10)
lambda_grid  <- 10^seq(-2, 5, length.out = 20)


validation_results <-
  purrr::imap(model_formulas, 
              # over the three hour s representations
              function(f, model_name) {
                purrr::map(lambda_grid, function(lambda) {
                  # applying ridgereg to all lambdas
                  # use the fit to predict on the validation data
                  fit <- ridgereg(formula = f,
                                data = train_data_imp,
                                lambda = lambda)
                  predictions <- predict(fit, newdata = validation_data_imp)
                  tibble::tibble(model = model_name,
                     lambda = lambda,
                     rmse = 
                       sqrt(mean((
                         validation_data_imp$arr_delay 
                         - as.numeric(predictions))^2)))
                  }) |>
                  purrr::list_rbind()
                }) |>
  purrr::list_rbind()

validation_results |>
    dplyr::mutate(
        rmse = sprintf("%.5f", rmse)
    ) |>
    print(n = 60)

#
# final fitting, using the combined data set and the factor representation for hours
train_val_data <- 
  dplyr::bind_rows(
  train_data_imp,
  validation_data_imp)

final_model <- 
  ridgereg(
  formula = model_formulas$factor,
  data = train_val_data,
  lambda = 0.01
)

```


## Prediction on the test data set


```{r}
test_predictions <- predict(
  final_model,
  newdata = test_data_imp
)

test_rmse <- sqrt(mean(
  (test_data_imp$arr_delay - as.numeric(test_predictions))^2
))

test_rmse
```

## Comparison with a nmean-prediction baseline

```{r}
baseline_prediction <- mean(train_val_data$arr_delay)

baseline_rmse <- sqrt(mean(
  (test_data_imp$arr_delay - baseline_prediction)^2
))

baseline_rmse


100 * (baseline_rmse - test_rmse) / baseline_rmse

test_r2 <- 1 - test_rmse^2 / baseline_rmse^2

test_r2
```

```{r}
#' Extract ridge regression coefficients
#'
#' @param object An object of class ridgereg
#' @param ... Additional arguments for compatibility with the generic
#'
#' @return A named numeric vector of regression coefficients
#'
#' @export
coef.ridgereg <- function(object, ...) {
  stats::setNames(
    as.numeric(object$beta_hat),
    rownames(object$beta_hat)
  )
}

tibble::enframe(
  coef(final_model),
  name = "predictor",
  value = "estimate"
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(estimate)))

```

```{r}
library(glmnet)

set.seed(739228)

# Use the same training observations
x_train <- stats::model.matrix(
  model_formulas$factor, train_val_data
)[, -1]

y_train <- train_val_data$arr_delay

x_test <- stats::model.matrix(
  model_formulas$factor, test_data_imp
)[, -1]

# Cross-validate glmnet on training + validation only
set.seed(739228)

cv_model <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
  x_train, y_train,
  alpha = 0,
  nfolds = 10
)

# Evaluate on the untouched test set
glmnet_predictions <- predict(
  cv_model,
  newx = x_test,
  s = "lambda.min"
)

glmnet_test_rmse <- sqrt(mean(
  (test_data_imp$arr_delay - as.numeric(glmnet_predictions))^2
))

glmnet_test_rmse
```

  custom_coef_scaled[predictor_names] / custom_fit$x_sd
